header: Date: 2025-07-10 | Time: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Redwood SE), Laura (Aurora Head of ML), Mark (Aurora CTO), Sanjay (Aurora Platform)
summary: Quarterly business review focusing on usage growth, cost spikes last month, reliability incidents in May, discussion of Dedicated pilot for predictable throughput, and alignment on roadmap + next steps for benchmarking and compliance docs.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs (latency, cost, SLA)
Batching, KV cache and quantization recommendations
transcript: [00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? I have Priya and Ethan on from Redwood.
[00:08] Laura: Laura here, hi. Mark and Sanjay are on as well, catching up on audio.
[00:15] Jesse: Awesome. Agenda — QBR: usage, cost, reliability, roadmap and pilot conversation. Is that right, Priya?
[00:23] Priya: Yep, that's it. We'll keep it to 45 minutes and capture action items.
[00:30] Ethan: I'll be stepping through some latency numbers and a couple tuning ideas around batching and KV cache at the end.
[00:35] Mark: Great. We pushed more traffic in late May and saw some cost spikes and a couple tail-latency issues, so want to unpack that.

[00:45] Jesse: Totally. Quick overview — Aurora's tokens per day has grown ~3x over the last quarter; cost per thousand tokens increased because of longer context and a small number of heavy users hitting long sequences.
[00:58] Laura: Yeah, our new summarization flow sends full transcripts as prompts. We didn't fully account for context window growth.
[01:10] Sanjay: Also we moved some traffic to eu-west without changing routing policies, so there was a mismatch in model variant and some fallback to the hosted pool, which spiked unit costs.
[01:26] Jesse: Right — smart routing + region pinning would help. We can route by policy so those EU requests hit a cheaper model variant or your Dedicated pool if you want predictability.
[01:40] Mark: Can you remind us the Dedicated tradeoffs? Cost vs latency vs isolation?

[01:46] Priya: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, predictable throughput, and data isolation. It costs more in commit but unit cost for heavy steady workloads tends to be lower and latency is more stable.
[01:58] Laura: Any rough numbers for our usage? We want to see run-rate comparisons — hosted token unit cost vs Dedicated commit.

[02:05] Jesse: We'll send a 90-day cost breakdown with modeled Dedicated pricing. Initial look: with steady 3x growth, Dedicated starts to look better once you exceed around X tokens/day — we'll quantify in the follow-up.

[02:22] Ethan: On reliability — you mentioned tail latency in May. We pulled traces: many long tails correlate with cold KV cache misses and very long prompt sequences causing multiple attention recomputations.
[02:36] Sanjay: There were two incidents: May 12th ~ 45m of degraded p99, and May 27th a shorter 15m blip. Both aligned with large bulk jobs from one internal team.

[02:49] Jesse: For that, we recommend a combination: prefix caching for repeated system prompts, client-side rate limiting for large bulk jobs, and enabling our continuous batching mode with a lower max latency target.
[03:05] Laura: Is prefix caching safe for PII content? We have some compliance constraints.
[03:10] Priya: Yes, caching can be configured per-route and respects retention policies; also we can integrate with your KMS and tokenization rules so PII never gets cached if you opt out.
[03:23] Mark: Speaking of compliance, can you resend SOC2 and ISO docs? Our procurement needs them for the pilot approval.
[03:30] Priya: Absolutely — I'll share the SOC2/ISO attestation and our security summary after this call.

[03:36] Ethan: On performance tweaks, quantization tradeoffs are worth discussing. We can suggest lower-precision variants for cheaper inference for non-critical prompts while keeping higher-precision for your gold-path.
[03:51] Laura: We did notice a few small regressions in output quality when we tried a 4-bit config last month — we have a set of prompts that are sensitive.
[03:58] Jesse: Good note — for the pilot we can do A/B: run sensitive prompts on high-precision models and bulk cheaper requests on quantized profiles. We'll help set guardrails and evals.
[04:12] Mark: What's involved to start a Dedicated pilot? Timeline and infra work?

[04:18] Priya: Typically we kickoff with a 2–4 week benchmarking window, validate latency and throughput, then agree on a commit size. For Aurora we also recommend a short private VPC connectivity test if you want network controls.
[04:33] Sanjay: We prefer VPC peering on prem-ish — can you support private control plane and customer-managed KMS?
[04:40] Jesse: Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and a private control plane. For Dedicated we can also put the pools in your VPC depending on region and compliance.
[04:50] Laura: On monitoring, can we get per-route token breakdowns and error traces? Our SREs will need that for SLIs.
[04:56] Ethan: Console has token-level breakdowns and tracing hooks; we'll share a dashboard template. We can also set up alerting for p99/p999 latency thresholds and error rates.
[05:10] Mark: One concern — how opaque are the kernels/optimizations? We sometimes need to validate determinism for audits.
[05:18] Priya: We can provide a document summarizing kernel selection logic, determinism guarantees for given profiles, and audit logs for request handling.
[05:29] Laura: Ok, thanks. For the upcoming benchmarking, what data do you need from our side?

[05:34] Ethan: Ideally: representative prompt set (you mentioned five sensitive prompts), traffic patterns (QPS over day), and a couple of model flavors you want to test. Also any network constraints so we can simulate realistic latencies.
[05:47] Sanjay: We'll extract the prompt set and traffic windows and share by next Tuesday.
[05:52] Jesse: Perfect. Recap — action items: cost report, SOC2 docs, perf deep dive scheduling, and sample prompts. Any other blockers?
[06:00] Laura: Procurement needs an estimated monthly run-rate for Dedicated — that will unblock finance approvals. Please include ranges and assumptions.
[06:07] Jesse: We'll include optimistic/expected/pessimistic run-rate scenarios and assumptions about batching and quantization.
[06:15] Mark: One quick follow — we sometimes route to a third-party re-ranker (Pinecone-ish) — any integration concerns?
[06:23] Ethan: We integrate fine with external re-rankers; just watch for cross-system latencies and tokenization differences. We'll include best practices in the benchmarking doc.
[06:34] Laura: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[06:38] Priya: No, thanks everyone. We'll send the documents and set up the benchmarking slot.
[06:44] Jesse: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the cost model and draft SOW for a Dedicated pilot. Meeting adjourned.
[45:00] <end of recording>
